subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@acmeretail.com>, Tom Chen <t.chen@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Hi Lara and Tom,

Thanks again for the call today — great to learn more about Acme Retail's search/QA needs. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the POC/trial so we can align on scope and timelines: 

Summary of goals
- Primary success criteria: 85%+ top-1 relevance for product search queries (measured on the provided evaluation set) and average response latency under 450ms for 95th percentile in our Dedicated test harness.
- Secondary: good multilingual support for EN/ES/PT product titles/descriptions.

POC scope & evaluation plan
1) Models to evaluate (initial):
   - Mistral-Instruct-7B (baseline: instruct-tuned open model, fast decoding)
   - Llama-2-13B (quantized to 4-bit for cost/quality tradeoff)
   - Fallback: Llama-2-7B (lower-cost fallback for heavy traffic)

2) Data and metrics
   - We'll run on your 2k sample queries + holdout 1k eval set (you shared Data-Sample.csv).
   - Metrics: top-1 accuracy (relevance), MRR, latency p95, and token cost per 1k requests.

3) Timeline & ownership
   - Week 1 (Sep 13–17): infra + model selection + baseline runs (Redwood: Aditya, Jordan).
   - Week 2 (Sep 20–24): fine-tuning/instruction-tuning prompts + evaluation (Redwood: Aditya; Acme: Lara for label review).
   - Week 3 (Sep 27–Oct 1): performance tuning (batching/quantization) and final eval report.

4) Deliverables
   - Weekly evaluation report, config artifacts, and runbook for production rollout.

Immediate asks for Acme
- Confirm the 1k held-out evaluation file and permission to use anonymized logs for metric calcs.
- Indicate language breakdown for queries (approx % EN/ES/PT).

I've attached a short PoC requirements sheet and the sample file you shared for reference. If this looks good, I'll schedule the infra kickoff with Aditya and Jordan.

Attachments:
- PoC-Requirements.xlsx (xlsx)
- Data-Sample.csv (csv)

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@acmeretail.com>

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Thanks Marissa — this is perfect and aligns with our expectations. A few quick clarifications: 

- Language mix: roughly 70% EN, 20% ES, 10% PT across queries.
- We can share the 1k holdout by end of day Monday (Sep 13).
- Regarding fallback: the main priority during peak is cost control; if Llama-2-7B can reduce token cost without large quality regression that's acceptable.

We give Redwood permission to run anonymized logs for metric calculation (we'll confirm with privacy/legal but ok to proceed).

Please go ahead and schedule the infra kickoff — call that week works for our engineering lead (Tom) as long as it's not before 11:00 PT.

Thanks,
Lara
Head of Search, Acme Retail
lara.gomez@acmeretail.com

Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan

Jordan/Aditya — heads up on the Acme POC. Key points:
- Languages: EN 70 / ES 20 / PT 10.
- Primary targets: Mistral-Instruct-7B and Llama-2-13B (quantized). Fallback Llama-2-7B for cost.
- Timeline: kickoff week of Sep 13. Lara says Tom (eng) is available after 11:00 PT.

Action items:
- Aditya: can you confirm the baseline infra config (GPU spec + quantized runtime) and estimated cost for week 1 runs? Also note any limitations around Spanish/Portuguese tokenizers and whether we should use a different tokenizer or language-specific prompt templates.
- Jordan: please prep a short agenda for the kickoff and own scheduling with Lara/Tom.

I'll schedule the kickoff tentatively Sep 14 11:30 PT and send an invite; feel free to propose alternatives.

Cheers,
Marissa

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lara Gomez <lara.gomez@acmeretail.com>, Tom Chen <t.chen@acmeretail.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC trial: model selection & evaluation plan (tech notes)

Thanks Marissa — quick technical notes and confirmations before kickoff: 

1) Baseline infra
- We'll provision a single Dedicated instance with an A100x1 equivalent for initial runs (good balance for 13B quantized evals). For the Mistral-7B baseline we can run on a T4-class for faster throughput/cost.
- Config: 1xA100 (13B quantized experiments), 1xT4 (Mistral-7B baseline), 16GB KV cache reserved.

2) Quantization & tokenizer
- Plan: run Llama-2-13B in 4-bit quantized mode (we use aware kernels to preserve quality). We'll validate generation quality on ES/PT. Tokenizers: tokenizer is BPE-based and supports ES/PT; however we should add language-specific prompt templates to normalize titles/descriptions (strip diacritics only as needed).

3) Fallback policy
- Implement smart routing: use Llama-2-13B by default; when concurrency > 200rps or latency SLO at risk, automatically route to Llama-2-7B. Redwood runtime will keep prefix cache warmed for both variants to reduce cold-start impact.

4) Eval harness & metrics
- We'll instrument the run with token-level cost and latency p50/p95. Deliverable: a Jupyter-friendly report + raw run artifacts.

5) Risks/asks
- Need the 1k holdout by Monday and a small set of labeled relevance judgments (~200) for quick sampling.
- Confirm whether any PII redaction is required before we ingest logs.

I'll bring a short technical checklist to the kickoff. If you want, I can prep the baseline run config as a JSON artifact beforehand and paste into the HubSpot record.

-Aditya
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
